I do not now say all this in order to launch a cheap
accusation against a system which has collapsed, but in
order to warn all men to open their eyes and see on what a
precipitous slope modern life in general has been moving.
The false doctrines of the "national-socialist" system are only
an extreme radical consequence of that development which
has been taking place in recent decades, in fact during the
whole of the past century. The belief in spiritual values has
faded more and more. A nationalistic will to power has
increasingly controlled political thought. Considerations of
utility, of practical advancement and profit, have in-
creasingly moulded education, the choice of a profession and
the conduct of life in general. The question of what a young
man should learn has been more and more considered from
the point of view: can it be of use to him later in life? That
has been asked rather than such primary questions as: Will
it develop his mind? Will it give to his life a content inde-
pendent of practical success, a content which will guard him
against temptation and raise him above the vexations and
disappointments of life? How often has there been talk of a
knowledge which is remote from the practical concerns of
life! It easily occurs to everyone that knowledge deviates
from life and chases vain fantasies. But to whom does it
occur that life itself may often in one way or another stray from
the truth which in the realm of knowledge is honoured as guide?
A life which is successful from the practical point of view
is far from being a life which deserves to be called a genuinely
human life. And knowledge is not remote from life simply
because it yields no results of apparent practical consequence,
and because its exponents appear in the eyes of the so-called
virtuosos of life to be unpractical dreamy men. Aloofness
from the world may also be an honour if the world voices the
criticism! And in the concerns of unpractical knowledge
true human life may be better preserved than in the life of
